newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - M1 nears 10 pct of Singapore handphones.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - M1 nears 10 pct of Singapore handphones.

text.p: Singapore's second mobile phone operator, MobileOne (M1), said on Thursday it had already grabbed almost 10 percent of Singapore handphone customers only three weeks after the market was deregulated.
Neil Montefiore, M1's chief executive officer, told Reuters in an interview the response to Mobileone had been "overwhelming".
"I don't want to use the word overwhelming, but the response has been way beyond our expectations," he said.
"In this first three weeks we must be the most successful entrant into any cellular market either initial, or second, or third, or whatever," Montefiore added.
MobileOne is a joint venture of Singapore Press Holdings, Keppel Telecom, Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications.
It was allowed on April 1 to offer the first rival handphone service to the former monopoly Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
Montefiore said M1 now had more than 35,000 customers in a market estimated at around 360,000 to 380,000 and was on target to break the 10 percent barrier by the end of the month.
"I think that's quite dramatic," he said.
